questions.name: kind
questions.instructions: Which kind of datapoint is this segment? Pick the one whose main point it makes. If it is scene-setting, general background, an opinion without evidence, a definition, a transition or filler, with nothing concrete to check, pick other.

criteria.stats: A measured number is the point: a count, amount, percentage, rate, price or size stated about one subject.
criteria.chart: Numbers for two or more things or periods set side by side to compare or trend: A versus B, before and after, up from X to Y, a series over years.
criteria.timeline: A specific event or action pinned to a date, year or sequence: what happened and when (founded, opened, voted, signed, died, expected).
criteria.quote: Words attributed to a named person or source: a direct quotation or reported speech.
criteria.findings: A conclusion established by evidence: what an audit, study, investigation or analysis found, showed, determined or concluded.
criteria.threads: A link between people, groups, events or documents (who funded, advised, reported to or caused whom), or an open lead or unanswered question to follow up.
criteria.callout: A key takeaway, warning, recommendation, risk or caveat the reader must not miss.
criteria.profile: Who or what a named person, organisation or place is: role, background, affiliation, size or purpose.
criteria.sources: Identifies a document, report, record or archive by title, author, date or reference, as a citation.
criteria.other: None of the above: atmosphere, description, general or vague statements, opinion, definitions, transitions, filler.

questions.name: importance
questions.instructions: The segment is a datapoint of the given kind. How important is it for someone skimming the document for its key points?
criteria: Trivial: filler, transitions or minor detail.
Critical: a headline finding or central fact.
